headline: Etsy returns to profit as last year's impairment fades
summary_short: Etsy's Q1 2026 revenue rose 3.1% y/y to $631.3M (down 28.4% q/q on normal post-holiday seasonality) as GAAP net income swung to $69.7M ($0.60 diluted EPS) from a $52.1M loss a year ago, mainly because Q1 2025 carried a $101.7M Reverb goodwill impairment that did not recur.
summary_long: Q1 2026 revenue grew 3.1% y/y to $631.3M (down 28.4% q/q on normal post-holiday seasonality), driven by a 7.9% rise in services revenue (higher Etsy Ads price-per-click) and a 1.1% rise in marketplace revenue, partly offset by the divested Reverb business. Gross profit rose 2.5% y/y to $455.6M. GAAP net income swung to $69.7M (diluted EPS $0.60) from a $52.1M loss a year ago, mainly because Q1 2025 carried a $101.7M Reverb goodwill impairment that did not recur; G&A also fell on reversal of a Canadian digital-services-tax accrual. Cash and equivalents fell to $1,214.4M from $1,355.4M q/q on $145.2M of buybacks. No forward guidance is disclosed in the 10-Q.

drivers.explanation: Growth was driven primarily by a 7.9% rise in services revenue (higher average price-per-click on Etsy Ads) and, to a lesser extent, a 1.1% rise in marketplace revenue (payments and transaction fees), partly offset by lost Reverb revenue post-divestiture.
Gross profit growth follows revenue's 3.1% y/y rise outpacing a 4.7% increase in cost of revenue, driven by higher refund costs, payments fees, and cloud hosting/bandwidth expense.

The swing to profit is explained by the absence of the year-ago $101.7M Reverb goodwill impairment charge, plus an $11.4M decline in G&A from reversal of a Canadian digital-services-tax accrual after its March 2026 repeal.
